samples.summary: `selectPastedRange` switched to `rangeOf`, which spreads one argument per pasted cell into `Math.min`/`Math.max` — a large paste can throw RangeError (stack overflow)
samples.evidence: The removed code walked the grid keys with an explicit loop tracking minR/maxR/minC/maxC. The replacement calls `rangeOf(grid)` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:18-27), which does `Math.min(...rows)` / `Math.max(...cols)` with `rows.length === grid.size`. A paste of a large TSV/region (~100k+ non-empty cells, easily reachable for a 10k-row × 10-col external paste) exceeds V8's argument-spread limit and throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. This happens after `store.endBatch()`, so the data is written but `paste()` rejects, leaving the caller with an unhandled rejection and no selection update. `rangeOf` is used nowhere else in src (grep `rangeOf\(`), so nothing else exercised this on paste-sized inputs.

samples.summary: Cut-paste that overlaps its own source is falsely refused: `planPasteMerges` does not exempt the merges being moved, unlike `moveRangeTo`
samples.evidence: `planPasteMerges` refuses whenever any merge intersecting `destRange` is not fully contained: `if (replaced.some((m) => !isRangeInRange(m.range, destRange))) return undefined;` (line 2426-2429). For a cut, the copied blocks are removed at the source anyway (lines 2274-2281 push them into `replacedMerges`), so a source block that the destination only clips cannot be split — yet it triggers `merge-paste-partial`. `moveRangeTo` handles exactly this by filtering the destination check with `movedAnchors` (sheet.ts:2601-2605). Reachable example: cut A1:D4 containing merge C3:D4, paste at B4 → destRange B4:E7 clips C3:D4 → refusal with the misleading message "Unmerge the destination first", while the equivalent drag-move succeeds. Fails loudly with no corruption, but blocks a valid operation and is inconsistent with the sibling path.

samples.summary: Cut paste deletes source merges from a stale snapshot: a merge created at the same anchor after the cut is destroyed (and with the wrong span)
samples.evidence: On cut, `paste` pushes `this.copyBuffer.merges` (a snapshot taken at `cut()` time) into `replacedMerges`; `applyPasteMerges` then does `this.store.deleteMerge(merge.anchor)` / `this.merges.delete(anchorSref)` (lines 2467-2468) without re-checking the live map. If the user cuts A1:B1 (merged), then unmerges it and merges A1:A5 instead, the later paste deletes the *new* A1:A5 block, and the `changedSrefs` loop at 2464 iterates the stale span (A1:B1) so the real covered cells A2:A5 are never invalidated for recalculation. Losing an unrelated merge plus a stale-recalc window.

samples.summary: `clearCellsUnderMerge` skips cells the paste itself wrote, so a pasted merge can hide live content (invariant "covered cells hold no content" broken)
samples.evidence: `if (sref === anchorSref || written.has(sref)) continue;` (line 2504) assumes the written grid never contains a cell that a newly created merge covers. That holds only while the copy source respects the invariant. An external paste (which this change deliberately leaves merge-unaware, lines 2208-2212) writes through `setGrid` → `store.setGrid` with no anchor normalization (sheet.ts:990-992), so it can plant content in cells covered by an existing merge; copying that region (`fetchGrid` returns raw store cells, sheet.ts:1906) puts those covered srefs into `copyBuffer.grid`, and pasting re-creates the merge with hidden content underneath that reappears on unmerge.

samples.summary: An internal paste of an empty-but-merged range drops destination merges and re-creates the copied layout while writing no values, leaving the destination anchor's old value under the new block
samples.evidence: `if (!hasContent && sourceMerges.length === 0)` (line 2404) only short-circuits when there are also no merges. With `hasContent === false` and merges present, `setGrid(grid)` writes nothing, but `applyPasteMerges` still deletes every destination block and creates the copied ones; `clearCellsUnderMerge` skips the anchor (`sref === anchorSref`), so the destination anchor keeps its pre-existing value while the surrounding covered cells are wiped — the paste of a blank range silently destroys data around, and keeps data at, the anchor.

finding.summary: `selectPastedRange` switched to `rangeOf`, which spreads one argument per pasted cell into `Math.min`/`Math.max` — a large paste can throw RangeError (stack overflow)
finding.evidence: The removed code walked the grid keys with an explicit loop tracking minR/maxR/minC/maxC. The replacement calls `rangeOf(grid)` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:18-27), which does `Math.min(...rows)` / `Math.max(...cols)` with `rows.length === grid.size`. A paste of a large TSV/region (~100k+ non-empty cells, easily reachable for a 10k-row × 10-col external paste) exceeds V8's argument-spread limit and throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. This happens after `store.endBatch()`, so the data is written but `paste()` rejects, leaving the caller with an unhandled rejection and no selection update. `rangeOf` is used nowhere else in src (grep `rangeOf\(`), so nothing else exercised this on paste-sized inputs.

verdict.reason: The claim checks out in the repository. `rangeOf` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:18-27) maps every grid key to a ref and spreads the resulting arrays into `Math.min(...rows)`/`Math.max(...cols)`, so the argument count equals `grid.size`. `selectPastedRange` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2541-2555) calls it with only a `grid.size === 0` early return — no upper bound. The grid reaching it is unbounded: `paste()` (sheet.ts:2214-2295) builds it via `string2grid` (grids.ts:113-126, one entry per TSV cell) or `html2grid` (grids.ts:164-181, one per td/th), and I found no size cap anywhere in that path (grep for MAX_/LIMIT/limit turned up only MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES and an unrelated MAX_SAFE_INTEGER); `store.setGrid` (store/memory.ts:260-266) also does not truncate. A ~100k+ cell paste therefore spreads ~100k arguments and can throw RangeError. The call site is at sheet.ts:2376, after the try/finally closing with `store.endBatch()` (sheet.ts:2371-2373), so cells are already written while `paste()` rejects and the selection is never updated — a crash plus inconsistent state on a normal-use path. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, nothing guards grid size upstream, and a runtime crash / broken invariant is within the correctness lens.
